The property is 7.03 acres located east of Snickersville Turnpike and south of Philomont Road in the Countryside Residential 1 Zoning District in the Catoctin Election District.

The property is in the Rural Policy Area, in the Rural Historic Village Place Type, and the Village Conservation Overlay District. The applicant is requesting a commission permit to develop a new 18,800-square-foot fire and rescue station with associated site infrastructure and improvements.

This station will replace the existing Philomont Fire and Rescue Station, which is located a half mile to the northwest. The application also consists of a special exception request to allow a fire and rescue station facility in the CR1 zoning district. The rural historic village place type identifies public facilities such as a fire and rescue station as a conditional use within the place type, meaning they are evaluated on a case-by-case basis.

Staff finds the location of the proposed fire and rescue station is in general conformance with the land use policies of the 2019 General Plan and with the land use and design policies for the rural policy area. The 2019 general plan supports the preservation of the character of the villages and their historic structures and sites through the rehabilitation and adaptive reuse of existing buildings.

Adaptive reuse of the existing station would be more consistent with plan policy, but staff acknowledges that feasibility studies have been conducted to explore this option, and they were deemed not practical. Other than the existing and proposed fire station, the closest fire station to the village of Philomont is Aldi Station No. 7, located approximately 8.6 miles southwest from the subject parcel, and the Roundhill Fire Station No. 4, located approximately 6.9 miles to the north.

Staff acknowledged the need for public facilities such as fire and rescue stations and their importance in providing safety and welfare to communities. This is the existing commission permit, Platt. The submitted exterior renderings depict a large building that sits on a fieldstone foundation and is clad in a vertical boardwood siding.

Varying roof lines and intersecting blocks help to reduce the perceived mass of the building by dividing the building into smaller pieces as recommended by the Rural Historic Villages Design Guidelines. The design appears to draw inspiration from simple agricultural forms that are commonly seen throughout western Loudoun County.

Building materials include fiber cement siding, stone or alternative stone materials, fiber cement or PVC trim, and standing seam metal roof panels. The proposed design for the fire and rescue station includes materials and details that are similar to the agricultural buildings found throughout Philmont.

Staff finds no outstanding environmental or heritage resource issues with the applications. The project has been conditioned to provide low-impact development, best management practice measures, an oil and water separator, tree conservation area, invasive species control, the use of native species for landscaping, and a pollinator garden.

The application has been conditioned to minimize the visual, environmental, and heritage impacts of the proposed fire and rescue station. Staff supports board ratification of the commission permit, and staff supports board approval of the special exception.
